extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and institutional administrators (universities, museums, social-service organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Planning and executing publicity/propaganda campaigns for educational institutions, museums, social-service organizations and related institutional actors to shape public opinion, attract support, and communicate scholarly or civic work to the general public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold ethical standards and work in harmony with the press
rubrics_metrics.description: The Association endeavors to uphold the ethical standards of the profession and aims to work in harmony with the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicity bureaus should maintain professional ethics, cultivate cooperative relations with newspapers, and participate in collective professional activity (e.g., newsletters, associations) to sustain standards and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popularize scholarly research in forms the public can understand
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of their scholarly researches should not only be presented to libraries and learned publications, but should also, where practicable and useful, be given to the public in the dramatic form which the public can understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate technical findings into clear, dramatic narratives for general audiences (example: the Harvard professor whose Mayan calendar discovery reached popular press through a press agent). Use popularization to gain public interest in scholarly achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an official publicity office with a director and staff
rubrics_metrics.description: There is hardly a college or university in the country which does not, with the approval of the governing body and the faculty, maintain a publicity office, with a director and a staff of assistants, for the purpose of establishing friendly relations with the newspapers, and through the newspapers, with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutionalize publicity functions (formal office and personnel) with governing-body approval. Accept that this is a modern innovation breaking with old traditions of cloistered seclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: President must manage institutional public image and diagnose causes of bad impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: If his institution does not produce the mental picture which it should, one of two things may be wrong: Either the media of communication with the public may be wrong or unbalanced; or his institution may be at fault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional leaders should determine whether poor public perception stems from PR/media issues (fix messaging) or from institutional shortcomings (modify programs). The public relations counsel has responsibility to correct impressions or recommend substantive institutional change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure programs/products are communicable before promoting them
rubrics_metrics.description: If extension courses... have been badly planned, from the point of view of public relations, if they are unduly scholastic and detached, their effect may be the opposite of favorable. In such a case, it is not the work of the public relations counsel to urge that the courses be made better known, but to urge that they first be modified...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not simply advertise poorly conceived offerings; first adapt them so they are accessible and consistent with the public impression the institution seeks to create, while respecting scholastic ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct public misconceptions by high-spotting relevant activities
rubrics_metrics.description: If the general opinion that an institution's work is 80 per cent postgraduate research is false, it should be corrected by high-spotting undergraduate activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize and publicize specific activities that counter damaging misconceptions (selective highlighting of programs, events, or achievements). If the impression is true, publicize the strength instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicize discoveries of public interest and dramatize scientific relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Make known the discoveries which are of possible public interest... a zoological department... chasing bacilli is in itself capable of dramatic presentation to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify aspects of scholarly work with clear public relevance and present them dramatically to attract broader attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lend faculty to public investigations to increase institutional relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Many universities now gladly lend members of their faculties to assist in investigations of public interest. Thus Cornell lent Professor Wilcox to aid the government in the preparation of the national census. Professor Irving Fisher of Yale has been called in to advise on currency matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate faculty participation in public service and advisory roles to raise institutional profile and demonstrate public utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid abuse: do not overadvertise or create artificial values
rubrics_metrics.description: In the ethical sense, propaganda bears the same relation to education as to business or politics. It may be abused. It may be used to overadvertise an institution and to create in the public mind artificial values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize limits and ethical risks of propaganda; guard against exaggerated promotion that manufactures false values for institutional gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose venue strategically to maximize authority and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the purpose was to see the entire country, the association was advised to hold it in the South. For, said the propagandist, a point of view on a southern question, emanating from a southern center, would have greater authority than the same point of view issuing from any other locality...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select event locations and timing so they lend credibility and authority to the message (locality can strengthen the persuasive effect on national audiences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlist recognized leaders and local influencers to lend weight
rubrics_metrics.description: The third step was to surround the conference with people who were stereotypes for ideas that carried weight all over the country. The support of leaders of diversified groups was sought...it was particularly important from the technical standpoint to secure the opinions of group leaders of the South.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite nationally and locally respected figures to participate; secure endorsements or visible cooperation from recognizable authorities to broaden acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design events with dramatic elements to attract national attention
rubrics_metrics.description: A dramatic element was spot-lighted here and there. A national leader from Massachusetts agreed in principle and in practice with a Baptist preacher from the South.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure programs so they contain striking, quotable moments or symbolic demonstrations that editors and the public will notice and disseminate widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up events with targeted communications to extend publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Further publicity was attained by mailing reports, letters, and other propaganda to selected groups of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mailings, reports and targeted outreaches after events to consolidate gains and reach specific constituencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat social-service campaigns as behavior-change propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: A campaign for the preservation of the teeth seeks to alter people's habits... A campaign against tuberculosis is an attempt to convince everybody that tuberculosis can be cured... Social service, in fact, is identical with propaganda in many cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame social-service messaging as campaigns for habit and opinion change; design messages around clear behavioral objectives and practical guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build enlightened public opinion to enable governmental/administrative reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislature must be persuaded to permit the utilization of the best methods of scientific penology... The solution of prison problems, then, seems to be fundamentally a problem of conscientious and scientific publicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan PR aimed at shaping public opinion that in turn pressures political institutions to implement reforms or appropriate policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use associational authority (endorsements/partnerships) to lend credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Markets are developed by going to Paris for inspiration. Paris can give American silk a stamp of authority which will aid it to achieve definite position in the United States. The French Minister of Fine Arts may be induced to lend his authority to the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associate products, exhibitions or programs with recognized external authorities (international exhibits, prominent figures, museums) to transfer credibility and accelerate acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museums should interpret collections and project esthetic leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The museum’s accomplishments should not be evaluated merely in terms of the number of visitors. Its function is not merely to receive visitors, but to project itself and what it stands for in the community which it serves... It must boldly assume esthetic leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Museums should proactively translate and bring art to communities (lectures, loan collections, education programs) and consider councils or research boards to set community standards in decoration, architecture and applied arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage commercial partnerships (stores, exhibitions) to bring art to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Department stores took it up. R. H. Macy & Company held an Art-in-Trades Exposition... These stores, coming closely in touch with the life of the people, performed a propagandizing function in bringing to the people the best in art as it related to these industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner with retailers and commercial venues to expose broader publics to curated art/design and influence popular taste through accessible, mass-market channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor changing media values and exploit shifts immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: The important point to the propagandist is that the relative value of the various instruments of propaganda, and their relation to the masses, are constantly changing. If he is to get full reach for his message he must take advantage of these shifts of value the instant they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously evaluate media effectiveness (meetings, newspapers, radio, automobile, etc.) and adopt new channels quickly when they become consequential for reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize newsworthiness and accuracy when pitching to newspapers
rubrics_metrics.description: The real criterion governing the publication or non-publication of matter which comes to the desk is its news value... What the newspaper does strive for is that the news which it publishes shall be accurate, and (since it must select from the mass of news material available) that it shall be of interest and importance to large groups of its readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft releases and pitches with clear news value, accurate facts, and broad interest. Editors are independent and may reject material lacking these qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always state the source and present facts accurately to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: The source of the news offered to the editor should always be clearly stated and the facts accurately presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency of sourcing and factual accuracy are essential; misleading or anonymous claims risk immediate dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create genuine events (news) that can compete in editorial selection
rubrics_metrics.description: He creates some of the day’s events, which must compete in the editorial office with other events. Often the events which he creates may be specially acceptable to a newspaper’s public and he may create them with that public in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities that are authentic, newsworthy and tailored to the target outlet's readership so they stand a chance of editorial pickup (but be aware editors may still discard them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor material to magazines' continuous editorial policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The average magazine assumes no obligation, as the newspaper does, to reflect the current news. It selects its material deliberately, in accordance with a continuous policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When targeting magazines, align content to the magazine's ongoing themes (e.g., health, fashion, home decoration) and offer features that fit their deliberate selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize events' repercussion beyond the immediate audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The real value of the lecture, from the propaganda point of view, is in its repercussion to the general public. The lecture itself may be only a symbol, a ceremony; its importance, for propaganda purposes, lies in the fact that it was delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for secondary distribution channels (broadcast, press reports) so a local lecture or event produces national or widespread ripple effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for radio and broadcast formats; adapt buying and content strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: The radio is at present one of the most important tools of the propagandist. Its ability to reach millions of persons simultaneously naturally appeals to the advertiser... Whether, in the future, air space will be sold openly as such, or whether the message will reach the public in the form of straight entertainment and news, or as special programs for particular groups, the propagandist must be prepared to meet the conditions and utilize them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and adapt to changing broadcast business models (advertiser-paid vs. listener-paid, program vs. ad space). Plan both content and media-buy approaches for radio and emerging broadcast technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use motion pictures as mass carriers but recognize market-driven content
rubrics_metrics.description: The American motion picture is the greatest unconscious carrier of propaganda in the world to-day. The motion picture can standardize the ideas and habits of a nation. Because pictures are made to meet market demands, they reflect, emphasize and even exaggerate broad popular tendencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ film/media to shape mass culture, but design expectations around the fact that movies typically reflect prevailing trends and market tastes rather than introduce radical new ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate and manage public personalities consistently and authentically
rubrics_metrics.description: The vivid dramatization of personality will always remain-one of the functions of the public relations counsel... Once a public figure has decided what ends he wishes to achieve, he must regard himself objectively and present an outward picture of himself which is consistent with his real character and his aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop authentic public personas that align with institutional aims; treat personality management objectively and avoid sensational misuse that can undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use repeated interpretation to accustom public to new inventions and change
rubrics_metrics.description: Propaganda assists in marketing new inventions. Propaganda, by repeatedly interpreting new scientific ideas and inventions to the public, has made the public more receptive. Propaganda is accustoming the public to change and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain messaging explaining new technologies/inventions over time to build public understanding and acceptance; repetition and interpretation are key to adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit technological dissemination aids (television, loud speakers) when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Television, broadcasting, loud speakers are utilized as propaganda aids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt appropriate dissemination technologies as they emerge, integrating them into strategy to broaden reach and adapt message formats.
